lessons.title: 1: PRODUCTIVITY TOOLS
topics: Overview
This topic introduces learners to essential productivity tools, with a primary focus on spreadsheets.
Learners will understand how software applications enhance efficiency in organising, calculating,
analysing, and presenting data across various contexts such as schools, offices, and homes. By the end
of this topic, learners will be able to perform fundamental data entry, analysis, and visualisation tasks.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Choose any of the following but not limited to:
Artificial (Physical – Classroom)
Classroom: Use board or charts to discuss spreadsheet components.
Charts and Posters: Display labelled spreadsheet parts.
Hands-On Demo: Learners explore spreadsheet software on computers.
Technology Environment
Computer Laboratory: Learners interact directly with spreadsheet tools.
assessment: Examples of Formative
Scenario: Your cousin Bwalya runs a small kantemba at Soweto Market in Lusaka. She sells vegetables such
as tomatoes, onions, and cabbage. She has an exercise book where she writes each day’s sales, but at the
end of the week, she spends hours adding everything with a calculator and often makes mistakes. She has
heard that a computer can help her.
(Data Entry & Interface) You open a blank spreadsheet for Bwalya. She looks at all the empty boxes

lessons.title: 2: DATA REPRESENTATION
topics: Overview
Data representation refers to the way data such as numbers, text, images, and sound are stored and
processed in a computer. Since computers only understand binary, different number systems and coding
schemes are used. This topic introduces learners to binary, denary, octal, and hexadecimal number
systems, and how text is represented using coding systems like ASCII.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Artificial (Physical – Classroom):
 Classroom arranged for group work with space to create posters.
 Clear view of board/projector for class discussion and comparison table.
Technology Environment:
 Optional: computers or tablets for reference or digital base charts.
 Projector/board to display examples of number systems.
Natural Environment:
assessment: Examples of Formative
Scenario: Your younger cousin in Chipata sees you working on a computer at a community centre
and asks, “Bakamba (Elder), I heard that computers only understand 0 and 1. But we are learning
about numbers like 10, 25, and 100 in school. How can a computer work with many school numbers
if it only knows two digits?”
(Binary/Denary) Explain to your cousin how the computer takes the number he sees (like 5)

lessons.title: 3: INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING
topics: Overview
This topic introduces learners to the fundamental concepts of programming through visual, block-based
environments. It focuses on how to think logically, sequence instructions, and create simple programs
using drag-and-drop coding blocks.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Artificial (Physical – Classroom):
 Classroom arranged for individual exploration and pair discussion
 Clear view of board/projector for demonstrations and comparisons
Technology Environment:
 Computers or laptops with internet access
 Block-based programming software: Scratch, Blockly, MIT App Inventor, Code.org
 Projector to show interface overview and examples
assessment: Examples of Formative

lessons.title: 5: CYBER SECURITY
topics: Overview
Cyber security focuses on keeping digital devices and information safe from threats such as viruses,
hacking, and online scams. In schools, homes, and workplaces in Zambia, people rely on computers and
mobile phones for communication and services. Learning cyber security helps learners protect their data,
avoid cybercrime, and use technology safely and responsibly.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Artificial (Physical – Classroom):
 Classroom arranged for small group discussions and board presentation
 Tables or desks grouped to allow collaboration
Technology Environment:
 Projector/board to display anonymised cybercrime stories, CIA Triad diagram, and examples
 Optional computers for learners to research additional local cyber incidents
Natural Environment:
assessment: Examples of Formative
Scenario: Your grandmother receives a text message: “Grandma, it’s me your grandson. I have lost my
phone. This is my new number. Please send me K200 for data so I can call you later.”
(Identifying Threats) What type of cyber threat is this message an example of?
(Policy Development) What are two specific pieces of advice you would give your grandmother to
help her avoid falling for this kind of trick in the future?

lessons.title: 6: ALGORITHMS
topics: Overview
This topic introduces learners to the fundamental principles of algorithms. Learners will explore how to
design, represent, and refine step-by-step procedures to solve computational and real-world problems.
Emphasis is placed on algorithmic thinking, logic development, and the use of visual tools like flowcharts
and pseudocode.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Artificial (Physical – Classroom):
 Classroom arranged for interactive discussion and pair work
 Open space at the front for demonstration (role-play of the nshima-making algorithm)
Technology Environment:
 Projector/board to display examples of algorithms (recipes, routines, GPS routes)
 Optional digital devices for viewing additional examples

lessons.title: 7: WEB DEVELOPMENT
topics: Overview
Web development involves the creation and styling of digital content to ensure it is functional, accessible,
and visually engaging. This topic focuses on Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), the essential design tool that
allows developers to control the presentation of HTML structures.
activities: Learning Environment Setup
Artificial (Physical – Classroom):
 Computer lab with individual workstations for learners
 Space for learners to implement CSS on HTML templates and share screens
Technology Environment:
 Computers with text editor (VS Code, Notepad++) and web browser
 Projector and screen to demonstrate CSS transformations
Natural Environment:
resources:  Colour blindness simulation tool (Spectrum or similar extension)
 Starter HTML/CSS page designed by learners for accessibility testing
 Worksheet to record observations, contrast ratio results, and responsive design issues
Suggested Teaching Methods
 Demonstration: Teacher shows how to use DevTools and extensions to test accessibility
 Hands-on Practice: Learners test their own pages for colour contrast, readability, and mobile

lessons.title: 8: DATABASES
topics: Overview
Databases are organised collections of data that allow for efficient storage, retrieval, and management of
information. This topic introduces Structured Query Language (SQL), the universal standard for interacting
with relational databases. Learners will move from understanding basic data organisation to designing
schemas and writing SQL scripts to create and modify database structures.
